root_cause.text: The function wbt_init_enable_default() in blk-wbt improperly uses WARN_ON_ONCE for expected and recoverable failure conditions (memory allocation failure in wbt_alloc() and -EBUSY from wbt_init()), which allows an attacker to trigger a spurious kernel warning by inducing memory pressure or other controllable failures.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that "wbt_alloc() can return NULL under memory pressure (-ENOMEM)" and "wbt_init() can fail with -EBUSY if wbt is already registered", and that syzbot triggers the warning by injecting memory allocation failures. The patch replaces WARN_ON_ONCE with plain if-checks and a pr_warn(), confirming that the warnings were inappropriate for these expected error paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak on wbt_init failure and replace unnecessary WARN_ON_ONCE with pr_warn to avoid spurious kernel warnings.
intent_record.what: In wbt_init_enable_default, removed WARN_ON_ONCE from allocation and init checks; added pr_warn and proper wbt_free on init failure.
intent_record.how: Previously, allocation failure triggered a kernel warning (WARN_ON_ONCE) and returned without warning on init failure (but also leaked memory). Now, allocation failure silently returns; init failure prints a warning via pr_warn and frees the allocated rwb structure, preventing memory leak and reducing unnecessary stack dumps.

grouping_result.intent: Fix memory leak on wbt_init failure and replace unnecessary WARN_ON_ONCE with pr_warn to avoid spurious kernel warnings.

candidates.rationale: Triggering a kernel warning on memory allocation failure is inappropriate because it is an expected recoverable condition. Inducing memory pressure can cause spurious warnings.
Triggering a kernel warning on wbt_init failure (e.g., -EBUSY) is inappropriate as it is an expected recoverable condition. Controllable factors can cause spurious warnings.

vuln_statements.explanation: Triggering a kernel warning on memory allocation failure (wbt_alloc returns NULL) is inappropriate because it is an expected, recoverable condition. An attacker can induce memory pressure to cause spurious warnings.
Triggering a kernel warning when wbt_init fails (e.g., returns -EBUSY) is inappropriate because it is an expected, recoverable condition. Controllable factors can cause spurious warnings.
